why:
phase-425 W3 -- subscribe `/clock` and install every sample as this image's ROS time, which is what rclcpp's `use_sim_time` parameter switches on. rclrs models ROS time as a `ClockSource` that a `Clock` is built `with_source`, so the override is driven by whoever owns the source and the `/clock` subscription is the application's to write; ours is an explicit verb on the node handle, for the same constraint `rust:Clock::ros_time` records -- with no allocator the source cannot be a separately-owned object shared between clocks, so the override is PROCESS-GLOBAL and an image has exactly one of it. Calling this on a second node adds a second subscriber to the same global, which is redundant rather than wrong. QoS is `QoSProfile::clock_default()` (= rclcpp's `ClockQoS`: best-effort, keep-last 1, volatile) because a late subscriber wants the NEXT sample and not a replay of the simulation's history; cancelling the returned handle stops the source and deliberately does NOT clear the override, so a node that unsubscribes mid-run keeps the last simulated time rather than jumping back to the wall clock. Behind the `sim-time` feature, which is why this row did not exist until 2026-09-12: `sim-time` was not in the parity extractor's `NROS_FEATURES`, so the subject was on no measured surface and the row could not be written at all. phase-430 W7 called these rows "still owed, deliberately" for exactly that reason -- issue 1351.

On `nros::Node`, the executor-borrowing node handle (`exec.node_mut(id)`); it was `NodeCtx` until phase-483 W2, which the correlator folded onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS`). MEASURABLE ONLY SINCE 2026-09-12: `nros_node::executor`'s `mod node` kept the type private while `Executor::node_mut` returned it, so every method on it was callable and none of them had ever produced a row -- issue 1351.
